quizzes.title: Fisheries Sector in India: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: India's fisheries sector is part of the agriculture and allied sectors, and it makes a notable contribution to agricultural output. The sector covers both capture fisheries and aquaculture, and India also exports seafood to buyers abroad. The government has launched several schemes to strengthen the sector. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana was introduced as part of the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Package, with the aim of bringing a Blue Revolution through the sustainable and responsible development of fisheries. Its focus areas include modernising fisheries infrastructure, promoting sustainable aquaculture practices, improving post-harvest management, and enhancing the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers. A sub-scheme under it, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana, supports micro and small enterprises operating in the sector and aims to formalise the sector under a national digital platform. The sector is also supported by integrated aqua parks, with parks planned in several states, and by a plan to develop climate resilient coastal fishermen villages. The scheme also aims to enhance fish production and productivity in India, to double farmers' income, and to coordinate fishery development in an integrated and holistic manner. A Fisheries Infrastructure Development Fund also envisages the creation of fisheries infrastructure in both marine and inland fisheries.

questions.q: According to the booklet, what percentage of agriculture Gross Value Added does the fisheries sector contribute?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that fisheries contribute 7.43% to agriculture GVA, the highest among agriculture and allied sectors.

questions.q: Which country is the largest importer of Indian seafood?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the United States as the largest importer of Indian seafood.

questions.q: In which year was the National Fisheries Development Board established?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the National Fisheries Development Board was established in 2006.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest population of river dolphins among the states surveyed.
Reason (R): The first riverine dolphin estimation was conducted to assess the population and conservation needs of river dolphins in India.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the survey's purpose stated in R does not explain why Uttar Pradesh has the highest population.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's fisheries sector:
I. The National Fisheries Development Board works under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
II. Fisheries is a State subject in India.
III. National Fish Farmers Day is observed on 21 November.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III confuses National Fish Farmers Day (July 10) with World Fisheries Day (Nov 21).

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about India's fisheries sector are correct?
I. The Matsya Setu App was launched by the NFDB and ICAR's Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture, Bhubaneswar.
II. Half of the Sah-Yojana investment comes from public finance, including the World Bank and the Agence Francaise de Developpement.
III. The Sagarmala Programme focuses on port-led development.
IV. The Sagarmala Programme focuses on fisheries education.
questions.explanation: Statements I to III match the booklet, while IV is wrong because the Sagarmala Programme focuses on port-led development.

quizzes.title: Fisheries Sector in India: TITA Practice
quizzes.passage: India's fisheries sector covers both capture fisheries and aquaculture, and it is supported by a range of government schemes. The National Fisheries Development Board is the nodal agency for the sector and works under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Its headquarters are in Hyderabad, Telangana. Fisheries is a State subject in India. The Board is involved in the Matsya Setu App, which was launched together with ICAR's Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture in Bhubaneswar to offer online training modules for fish farmers and stakeholders. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, introduced as part of the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Package, aims to modernise fisheries infrastructure and support sustainable aquaculture practices. Under it, a sub-scheme for micro and small enterprises in the sector seeks to formalise the sector under a national digital platform. The sector also includes five integrated aqua parks in several states and a plan to develop climate resilient coastal fishermen villages. A Fisheries Infrastructure Development Fund envisages infrastructure in both marine and inland fisheries, with lending through NABARD, the National Cooperative Development Corporation and scheduled banks. India's first riverine dolphin estimation was carried out to assess the population and conservation needs of river dolphins, and it recorded the highest population in Uttar Pradesh.

quizzes.title: WTO Fisheries Subsidies: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, also called the constitution for the oceans, sets out the legal framework within which all activities in the oceans and seas must be carried out. The UN High Seas Treaty, or BBNJ Agreement, is a legally binding international treaty governing ocean spaces beyond national jurisdiction. The high seas and the international seabed area are considered global commons, open to all states for activities such as navigation, overflight and laying of submarine cables and pipelines. The 1994 Agreement on Part XI deals with deep seabed mining, and the 1995 UN Fish Stocks Agreement is another implementing agreement under the Convention. The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference in 2022. Its objective is to establish binding rules that curb harmful fisheries subsidies. The agreement entered into force in September 2025, after two-thirds of members had approved it. It supports Sustainable Development Goal 14, which aims to conserve and sustainably use oceans, seas and marine resources. The WTO Fish Fund provides aid to developing and least developed country members for implementing the agreement. The International Seabed Authority has the mandate to ensure the effective protection of the marine environment from harmful effects that may arise from deep-seabed related activities.

questions.q: Under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, subsidies for fishing on which type of stocks are prohibited?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists subsidies for fishing on overfished stocks among the prohibited subsidies.

questions.q: Under the agreement, subsidies linked to which kind of fishing are prohibited?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that subsidies linked to IUU fishing are prohibited.

questions.q: Under the agreement, support for fishing in which area is prohibited?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists support for fishing in unregulated high seas as prohibited.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India has not joined the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies.
Reason (R): India has cited the need to protect small fishers, livelihoods and food security.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet gives protection of small fishers, livelihoods and food security as India's reason for not joining.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Obligation placed on members   ->   A. Submit fisheries-related data
II. Support for fishing on overfished stocks   ->   B. Prohibited
III. India's position on the agreement   ->   C. Did not join
IV. Treatment of developing countries   ->   D. Flexibility within common rules
questions.explanation: Members must submit fisheries-related data, subsidies for overfished stocks are prohibited, India did not join, and developing countries get flexibility within common rules.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies:
I. Subsidies for fishing on overfished stocks are prohibited.
II. Developing countries receive no flexibility under the agreement.
III. Members must submit fisheries-related data.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II contradicts the flexibility the booklet gives developing countries within common rules.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are correct?
I. Subsidies linked to IUU fishing are prohibited.
II. India has joined the agreement.
III. Support for fishing in unregulated high seas is permitted.
IV. Members must submit fisheries-related data.
questions.explanation: Statements I and IV match the booklet, while II and III are wrong.

quizzes.title: WTO Fisheries Subsidies: TITA Practice
quizzes.passage: The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, also called the constitution for the oceans, sets out the legal framework within which all activities in the oceans and seas must be carried out. The UN High Seas Treaty, or BBNJ Agreement, is a legally binding international treaty governing ocean spaces beyond national jurisdiction. Its core objective is to safeguard biodiversity in high seas areas beyond national jurisdiction. The high seas and the international seabed area are considered global commons, open to all states for activities such as navigation, overflight and laying of submarine cables and pipelines. The International Seabed Authority works to protect the marine environment from harmful effects of deep-seabed related activities. The Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf helps implement the Convention on the outer limits of the continental shelf. The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference. Its objective is to establish binding rules that curb harmful fisheries subsidies. The agreement prohibits support for fishing in unregulated high seas. It also requires members to submit fisheries-related data. Developing countries receive flexibility under the agreement, though within common rules. India did not join the agreement, citing the need to protect small fishers, livelihoods and food security.

questions.q: In which year was the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies adopted?
questions.explanation: The booklet links the agreement's adoption to the 12th Ministerial Conference in 2022.

questions.q: Which Sustainable Development Goal does the agreement support? (give the number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the agreement supports SDG 14 on conserving oceans, seas and marine resources.

questions.q: In which month and year did the agreement enter into force?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the agreement entered into force in September 2025.

questions.q: What fraction of members had to approve the agreement for it to enter into force? (in words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says entry into force followed approval by two-thirds of members.

questions.q: Which WTO fund provides aid to developing and LDC members for implementing the agreement?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the WTO Fish Fund as the source of implementation aid for developing and LDC members.

questions.q: Subsidies linked to which kind of fishing are prohibited? (give the acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that subsidies linked to Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated fishing are prohibited.

questions.q: Under the agreement, subsidies for fishing on which type of stocks are prohibited? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists subsidies for fishing on overfished stocks as prohibited.
